problem_name: Graph Sandwich Problem for a Pi-Property (decision)
canonical_encoding: two simple undirected graphs F, F' with F subset of F' (E(F) subset E(F')); target property Pi = being P_k-free (no induced path on k vertices) with k = Theta(|V|^{1/2})

simple undirected graph G, integer k (fixed k>=3); group chromatic number chi_g(G) = least l such that G is A-colorable for every Abelian group A of order >= l (A-colorable = for every orientation and every edge-labelling phi:E->A there is c:V->A with phi(u,v) != c(u)-c(v) on all arcs)
simple undirected graph G, integer k (fixed k>=3); G is hereditarily k-clique-colorable if it has a k-coloring that is a clique-coloring of G and of every induced subgraph of G
two integer expressions e1, e2 built from binary numerals with operators + and union; L(n)={n}, L(e+f)={a+b : a in L(e), b in L(f)}, L(e union f)=L(e) union L(f)
simple undirected graph G=(V,E), a partition (V_{i,j})_{i in I, j in J} of V, integer k; for t:I->J, f_t = size of a smallest vertex cover of G restricted to the union over i of V_{i,t(i)}

a set W with a partition (W_{i,j})_{i in I, j in J} of W, a set S of 3-element subsets of W, integer k; for t:I->J, f_t(W) = size of a largest matching (mutually disjoint triples) inside the union over i of W_{i,t(i)}
simple undirected graph G=(V,E), a partition (V_{i,j})_{i in I, j in J} of V, integer k; for t:I->J, f_t = size of the largest clique in G restricted to the union over i of V_{i,t(i)}
a 3-CNF formula phi(x,y) over two disjoint blocks of Boolean variables, integer k

simple undirected graph G=(V,E), integer k; a pebbling move removes 2 pebbles from a vertex and adds 1 to an adjacent vertex; pebbling number pi(G) = least k such that for every distribution of k pebbles and every target v there is a sequence of moves placing a pebble on v
a Boolean circuit (or Boolean formula) phi and an integer k; an implicant of phi is a set of literals whose conjunction implies phi, and its size is the number of literals
a well-formed Boolean formula phi over the basis {AND, OR, NOT}, integer k; |phi| = number of literal occurrences
a game in graphical normal form: players P, a neighbor set N(p) per player, an action set A(p), and a utility function u_p given as an explicit table over the joint actions of {p} union N(p)

simple undirected graph G=(V,E), integer k; a non-repetitive k-edge-coloring colors E with k colors so that along every path the sequence of colors is square-free (contains no block uu); Thue number = least such k
a set system over a finite universe U given SUCCINCTLY by a Boolean circuit C with C(i,x)=1 iff element x belongs to set S_i; integer k
a finite color set C including a blank color, a tile set T subset C^4 (sides top,right,bottom,left; no rotations or reflections; adjacent tiles must meet in equal colors), integer n (unary)
a collection S = {phi_1,...,phi_m} of 3-DNF formulas over n Boolean variables (each phi_i encodes its on-set, a subset of {0,1}^n), integer k

a propositional abduction problem (V,H,M,T): background theory T in CNF over variables V, hypotheses H subseteq V, manifestations M subseteq V; decision: does an explanation exist -- a set S subseteq H with T cup S consistent and T cup S |= M?

a set of autoepistemic premises (propositional formulas with the belief modality L) over n variables; a stable expansion is a fixed point of the expansion operator; decision: brave (credulous) reasoning -- does a query formula phi belong to some stable expansion?

a propositional theory T over n variables under (parallel) circumscription CIRC(T) selecting the subset-minimal models; decision: circumscriptive inference -- does CIRC(T) |= phi (phi holds in every subset-minimal model of T)?

a discrete competitive-location instance: clients with demands on a network/metric, candidate facility sites, integers p (leader) and r (follower); the leader opens p sites, then the follower opens r sites, each client patronizes the nearest open facility (ties to the leader); decision: can the leader capture demand >= t against the follower's best response?

problem_name: Credulous Acceptance in Abstract Argumentation (semi-stable semantics)
canonical_encoding: a Dung argumentation framework (finite directed graph of arguments + attacks); decision: is a given argument credulously accepted under semi-stable semantics -- in SOME semi-stable extension?

problem_name: Credulous Acceptance in Abstract Argumentation (stage semantics)
canonical_encoding: a Dung argumentation framework (finite directed graph of arguments + attacks); decision: is a given argument credulously accepted under stage semantics -- in SOME stage extension?

a propositional default theory (W,D): background W and a set D of defaults (prerequisite : justifications / consequent) over n variables; an extension is a Reiter fixed point; decision: brave (credulous) reasoning -- does a query phi belong to some extension?

a propositional disjunctive logic program (rules with disjunctive heads and default negation) over n atoms under the stable-model (answer-set) semantics; decision: consistency -- does the program have at least one answer set?

a judgment-aggregation scenario: an agenda of logically related propositions, a profile of individual consistent judgment sets, and an aggregation rule (e.g. a distance-based / ranked-agenda rule); decision variant of outcome determination: is a given proposition in the collective outcome?
a propositional CNF formula phi over n variables and a truth assignment M with M |= phi; decision: is M a subset-minimal model of phi (no model M' strictly-below M satisfies phi)?

a combinatorial optimization problem (e.g. selection / spanning-tree / shortest-path / knapsack) whose cost coefficients are given as intervals; a solution's regret in a scenario is its cost minus the scenario-optimum; decision: is there a feasible solution whose maximum regret over all interval scenarios is <= t?

a network with an interdiction budget: the leader (interdictor) removes/attacks <= b elements (edges/vertices), then the follower solves an [complexity-term-withheld] optimization X (e.g. shortest path or a knapsack-interdiction nominal problem) on the residual network; decision: can the leader force the follower's optimum past a threshold t?

a bilevel 0/1 (or bounded-integer) linear program: leader variables x, follower variables y, linear leader/follower objectives and joint linear constraints; the follower optimizes its own objective given x; decision: is there a leader x such that the induced follower-optimal (x,y) gives leader objective >= t?

a constraint satisfaction instance (variables, domains, constraints) and an integer k; a partial assignment to <= k variables is locally consistent if it violates no constraint; decision: robust satisfiability -- does EVERY locally-consistent size-<=k partial assignment extend to a full solution?
an undirected graph G with a distinguished set L of vertices and the palette {1,2,3}; decision: does EVERY proper 3-coloring of L extend to a proper 3-coloring of all of G?

problem_name: Skeptical Acceptance in Abstract Argumentation (semi-stable semantics)
canonical_encoding: a Dung argumentation framework (finite directed graph of arguments + attacks); decision: is a given argument skeptically accepted under semi-stable semantics -- in EVERY semi-stable extension?

problem_name: Skeptical Acceptance in Abstract Argumentation (stage semantics)
canonical_encoding: a Dung argumentation framework (finite directed graph of arguments + attacks); decision: is a given argument skeptically accepted under stage semantics -- in EVERY stage extension?

a two-stage robust combinatorial problem with discrete (budgeted Gamma-)uncertainty: first-stage 'here-and-now' variables are chosen, then an adversary picks a scenario from the budgeted uncertainty set, then second-stage 'wait-and-see' recourse variables are chosen; decision (min-max-min): is there a first-stage decision guaranteeing total cost <= t for every scenario's best recourse?

unobservable (no-sensing) planning: a set of possible initial states (belief state), actions with conditional/nondeterministic effects, expressive operator formalism; decision: does one fixed action sequence reach the goal from every possible initial state?
a Computation Tree Logic (CTL) formula over atomic propositions with path quantifiers A/E and temporal operators X,F,G,U; decision: is it satisfiable in some Kripke structure?

an n x n checkers (draughts) position on a generalized board; decision: does the player to move have a winning strategy under standard checkers rules?

an n x n chess position on a generalized board and piece set; decision: does the player to move have a winning strategy under chess rules (with a repetition/draw convention giving at most exponential game length)?

canonical_encoding: an n x n Go position under Japanese rules (with ko); decision: does the player to move have a winning strategy?
an n x n Gomoku/Gobang position (place stones, first to a fixed-length row wins); decision: does the player to move have a winning strategy?

problem_name: Generalized Hex (Shannon vertex game on graphs)
canonical_encoding: an undirected graph with two distinguished vertices s,t; two players alternately claim unclaimed vertices; decision: does the player trying to complete an s-t path of claimed vertices have a winning strategy?

a graph G and two independent sets I_s, I_t of equal size (token placements); decision: can I_s be transformed into I_t by single-token moves (slide to an adjacent vertex, or jump to any vertex) with every intermediate set independent?
a propositional formula over ->, &, v, not; decision: is it intuitionistically valid (provable in intuitionistic propositional calculus / valid in all Kripke models)?
a Linear Temporal Logic formula over atomic propositions with operators X (next), U (until), F, G; decision: does some infinite trace (omega-word model) satisfy it?
a propositional modal formula with box/diamond, interpreted over the basic normal modal logic K (equivalently T or S4); decision: is it satisfiable in a Kripke frame of the corresponding class?
a nondeterministic finite automaton N over alphabet Sigma; decision: is L(N) = Sigma* (does N accept every string)?

an undirected graph; two players alternately pick a vertex non-adjacent to all previously picked vertices (jointly building a maximal independent set); the player unable to move loses; decision: does player 1 have a winning strategy?

a constraint graph with weight-1 and weight-2 edges, each vertex requiring incoming weight >= 2; a move reverses one edge while keeping every vertex constraint satisfied; decision: is there a move sequence that reverses a target edge?
a first-order sentence over (natural numbers; +, =, <, constants) with quantifiers ranging over the integers; decision: is the sentence true?

a propositional STRIPS instance: initial state, goal, and ground operators (precondition / add / delete lists over Boolean state variables); decision: does a plan (sequence of applicable operators reaching the goal) exist?

a constraint satisfaction instance whose variables carry an alternating exists/forall quantifier prefix over a fixed finite domain; decision: is the quantified sentence true (does the existential player have a winning strategy)?
two regular expressions over a fixed alphabet built from union, concatenation, and squaring (e^2 abbreviates e.e, giving succinct exponentiation); decision: do they denote different languages?

a CNF (or Schaefer-type) formula and two satisfying assignments s,t; decision: is there a path from s to t in the solution graph (flip one variable per step, every intermediate assignment satisfying)?

a Boolean formula with a prefix of alternating existential and randomized (probability-p) quantifiers; decision: is there a strategy for the existential variables making the formula satisfied with probability >= theta?

a graph on 2^n vertices given succinctly by a Boolean circuit that, on a pair of vertex indices, outputs whether that edge is present; decision: does the represented graph contain a Hamiltonian cycle?
a CNF formula with 2^n clauses/variables given succinctly by a Boolean circuit that, on a clause index and literal slot, outputs the literal; decision: is the represented formula satisfiable?

problem_name: Skeptical Acceptance in Abstract Argumentation (preferred semantics)
canonical_encoding: a Dung argumentation framework (directed graph of arguments + attacks); decision: is a given argument skeptically accepted — in EVERY preferred extension?
a directed graph with a start vertex; two players alternately extend a simple path; a player unable to move loses; decision: does player 1 have a winning strategy?
a two-level (leader/follower) 0/1 knapsack with binary-encoded weights and profits; decision: can the leader guarantee objective >= t against the follower's optimal response?

problem_name: Three-Dimensional (Axial) Assignment Problem, metric perimeter costs (minimization)
canonical_encoding: complete tripartite structure on three n-sets; a feasible solution is a set of n disjoint triples (one element per set); objective = minimize total triple cost. Costs pinned METRIC (perimeter/decomposable: cost of a triple = sum of pairwise distances in an underlying metric), so the ratio is well defined (general arbitrary-cost 3AP allows 0-cost optima and is [complexity-term-withheld] in the strong sense).

3m positive integers a_1..a_{3m} with sum m*B and each B/4 < a_i < B/2; decision: can they be partitioned into m triples each summing exactly to B? (numbers may be given in unary — strong NP-completeness)
simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; objective = maximum k such that G has a proper k-coloring in which every pair of colour classes is adjacent (a complete colouring)
simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; objective = minimum number of colours in a proper vertex colouring with no bichromatic cycle (every 2-coloured induced subgraph is a forest)

problem_name: Art Gallery / Minimum Vertex-Guard Set (simple polygon)
canonical_encoding: a simple polygon P (possibly with holes) given by its vertex coordinates; guards placed at polygon VERTICES; a point is guarded if some guard sees it (segment inside P); objective = minimum number of vertex guards covering P. Vertex-guard variant pinned (keeps the decision in NP).
simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; objective = maximum k such that G has a proper k-colouring in which every colour class contains a vertex adjacent to all other k-1 classes (a b-colouring)

connected vertex-weighted graph, adjacency-list; partition V into q parts each inducing a CONNECTED subgraph; objective (max-min version) = maximize the weight of the lightest part. q pinned as part of the input.
simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; find a minimum vertex set S whose removal leaves every connected component with at most 2|V|/3 vertices; objective = minimize |S|
simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; a linear layout is a bijection f: V -> {1..n}; objective = minimize the bandwidth max_{uv in E} |f(u)-f(v)|
a ground set and a collection of ordered betweenness constraints (a,b,c) meaning 'b lies strictly between a and c'; decision: is there a total order of the ground set satisfying ALL constraints?

problem_name: Minimum Biclique Cover (edge cover by bicliques)
canonical_encoding: simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; cover every edge of G by complete bipartite subgraphs (bicliques); objective = minimum number of bicliques whose union contains all edges

a finite list of domino pairs (u_i, v_i) of strings over an alphabet, and a bound k (in unary); decision: is there a nonempty sequence of at most k indices i_1..i_t (t <= k) with u_{i_1}...u_{i_t} = v_{i_1}...v_{i_t}?

simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; objective = minimum dimension d such that G is the intersection graph of axis-parallel boxes in R^d (equivalently, the min number of interval graphs whose intersection is G)

simple undirected graph, adjacency-list, with a source vertex s; in each round every informed vertex may call one uninformed neighbour (telephone model); objective = minimum number of rounds to inform all vertices

simple undirected graph with a vertex capacity function c; a capacitated dominating set is a set D plus an assignment of every vertex not in D to a neighbour in D so that no v in D is assigned more than c(v) vertices; objective = minimize |D|

a metric on facilities and clients, facility opening costs, and facility capacities (max clients per open facility); objective = minimize (sum of opening costs + sum of client-to-assigned-facility distances) respecting capacities
simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; objective = minimum number of labels k in a clique-width expression (using disjoint union, relabelling, and label-join operations) that constructs G
a set of m strings of equal length L over a finite alphabet; objective = minimum radius d such that some string s has Hamming distance <= d to every input string
a set of m strings over a finite alphabet, and a target length L; objective = minimum radius d such that some length-L string s has Hamming distance <= d to a length-L SUBSTRING of every input string

problem_name: Cluster Deletion (edge deletion to disjoint cliques, minimization)
canonical_encoding: simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; objective = minimum number of edges to DELETE so that every connected component of the result is a clique (a cluster graph)

problem_name: Connectivity Augmentation (increase edge-connectivity by one, minimization)
canonical_encoding: a k-edge-connected graph G plus a set of candidate links (extra edges); objective = minimum-cardinality subset of links whose addition makes G (k+1)-edge-connected (Tree Augmentation is the k=1 special case)
a directed graph with two nonnegative edge functions cost and resource, a source, a target, and a resource budget R; objective = minimum-cost s-t path whose total resource use is <= R
simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; objective = minimum number of edge crossings over all drawings of G in the plane
simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; objective = maximum number of pairwise vertex-disjoint cycles (of any length >= 3)
a ground set and a collection of ordered triples (a,b,c); decision: is there a cyclic (circular) order of the ground set such that in every triple, going clockwise from a one meets b before c?

simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; a dissociation set induces a subgraph of max degree <= 1; its complement is a 3-path vertex cover (hits every path on 3 vertices). Pinned optimization object: minimize the 3-path vertex cover |S| = n - dissociation number (the well-behaved covering ratio).
simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; objective = maximum number of pairwise-disjoint dominating sets into which V can be partitioned (bounded above by min-degree + 1)

simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; a set D is efficient-dominating (a perfect code) if every vertex is dominated by EXACTLY one member of D (the closed neighbourhoods of D partition V); decision: does an efficient dominating set exist?

simple undirected graph, adjacency-list, and an integer k; a proper k-colouring is equitable if the colour-class sizes differ by at most one; decision: does G have an equitable k-colouring? (objective version: minimum such k)
n points in the Euclidean plane R^2 (fixed dimension d=2); objective = minimum-length closed tour visiting all points, distances = Euclidean (L2)

a metric on facilities and clients, and facility opening costs (no capacity limits); objective = minimize (sum of opening costs of opened facilities + sum of each client's distance to its nearest opened facility)
rooted tree, one firefighter per round protecting one vertex; fire spreads to unprotected neighbours; objective = maximize number of vertices saved (never burned)
n jobs, each processed on 3 machines in the fixed order M1->M2->M3 with given processing times; objective = minimize makespan (Cmax)
n items, m capacitated bins; item i in bin j has size s_ij and profit p_ij; assign a subset of items to bins respecting capacities; objective = maximize total profit
list of axis-parallel rectangles r_i=(w_i,h_i) with w_i,h_i in (0,1]; pack (no rotation, no overlap) into minimum number of unit square bins
set P of n points in the plane; cover all points using a minimum number of unit (radius-1) disks with free centres

problem_name: Maximum Independent Set of Unit Disks
canonical_encoding: set of n unit disks in the plane (a unit-disk graph); objective = maximum subset of pairwise non-intersecting disks
simple undirected graph; in each round the existing fire spreads to all neighbours and one new vertex is ignited; objective = minimum #rounds (burning number b(G)) to burn every vertex
simple undirected graph; objective = minimum genus g of an orientable surface in which G embeds without crossings
fixed simple graph H (non-bipartite, loopless); input a simple graph G; decision: does a homomorphism G->H exist?
simple undirected unweighted graph; objective = minimum-edge spanning subgraph H such that d_H(u,v) <= 2*d_G(u,v) for all u,v (a 2-spanner)
simple undirected graph; the Grundy number Gamma(G) = largest k such that some vertex ordering forces the greedy (first-fit) colouring to use k colours; objective = Gamma(G)
simple undirected graph; a proper colouring in which every pair of colours appears on at most one edge; objective = minimum number of colours (harmonious chromatic number)

problem_name: Independent Dominating Set (Minimum Maximal Independent Set)
canonical_encoding: simple undirected graph; a set S that is both independent and dominating (equivalently a maximal independent set); objective = minimum |S| (the independent domination number)
an integer expression over singleton constants using the operators union and pairwise sum (+); a target integer t; decision: is t in the set of integers denoted by the expression?

problem_name: Interval Graph Completion (minimum fill to an interval graph)
canonical_encoding: simple undirected graph G; objective = minimum number of edges to add so that the result is an interval graph
n jobs, each given as a set of candidate time intervals; select at most one interval per job so that selected intervals are pairwise disjoint; objective = maximize number of selected jobs
simple undirected graph G and integer k; objective = minimum-cardinality spanning subgraph that is k-edge-connected (unweighted, uniform requirement)
undirected graph with non-negative edge weights and integer k; objective = minimum-weight tree spanning at least k vertices

bipartite constraint graph, label sets L_U,L_V, each edge carrying a projection constraint pi_e: L_U->L_V; objective = a labelling maximizing the fraction of satisfied edges (the two-prover / PCP projection game)
simple undirected graph G with a list L(v) of admissible colours at each vertex; decision: is there a proper colouring c with c(v) in L(v) for all v?
n point sites in the plane; place an axis-parallel square label of common side length sigma at each site (fixed-position model), pairwise non-overlapping; objective = maximize sigma
CNF formula with clauses of exactly 2 literals; objective = maximum number of simultaneously satisfiable clauses
complete graph on n points with edge weights satisfying the triangle inequality, and integer p; objective = choose p points maximizing the sum of pairwise distances among them
CNF formula with clauses of exactly 3 distinct literals; objective = maximum number of simultaneously satisfiable clauses
simple undirected graph (optionally with non-negative edge weights) and integer k>=2; objective = partition vertices into k parts maximizing the total weight of edges crossing between parts

problem_name: Maximum Agreement Forest (two rooted binary trees)
canonical_encoding: two rooted binary phylogenetic trees on the same leaf label set; objective = an agreement forest with the fewest components (equivalently the rooted SPR distance = #components - 1)

problem_name: Maximum Constraint Satisfaction (MAX-CSP, Boolean fixed constraint family)
canonical_encoding: a fixed finite set F of Boolean relations; input a set of constraints each applying some relation from F to a tuple of variables; objective = maximum number of simultaneously satisfiable constraints
a system of linear relations (equations/inequalities) with rational coefficients that is infeasible as a whole; objective = maximum-cardinality subsystem that is feasible
simple undirected graph; an induced matching is a matching M whose edges induce no other edges (pairwise at distance >= 2); objective = maximum |M|
simple undirected graph; objective = maximum-cardinality MINIMAL vertex cover (a vertex cover no proper subset of which is a vertex cover)
simple undirected graph G; objective = maximum-cardinality edge subset E' such that the subgraph (V,E') is planar

problem_name: Minimum Routing Cost / Communication Cost Spanning Tree
canonical_encoding: connected graph with metric edge lengths; uniform (unit) communication requirement between every vertex pair; objective = spanning tree T minimizing routing cost = sum over all pairs of the T-path length (minimum routing cost spanning tree, MRCT). Encoding PIN: the uniform-requirement metric special case of the Optimum Communication Spanning Tree (OCT)
simple connected graph, adjacency-list; objective = spanning tree minimizing the maximum vertex degree
simple undirected graph; objective = a bijection f: V -> {1..n} minimizing sum over edges {u,v} of |f(u)-f(v)|
CNF formula (optionally weighted clauses); objective = truth assignment MINIMIZING the number (weight) of satisfied clauses
set system (universe of elements, family of sets); objective = a linear order on the sets minimizing the sum over elements of the cover time (index of the first set covering the element)
two strings that are permutations of each other; objective = a minimum-cardinality partition of each into blocks such that the two block multisets are equal (a common partition)

two finite sets of strings S+ (accept) and S- (reject) over a fixed alphabet; objective = a deterministic finite automaton with the fewest states that accepts every string in S+ and rejects every string in S-

a set of objects and a set of binary tests (each test splits the objects); objective = a decision tree of minimum cost (e.g. minimum total external path length / expected #tests) that identifies every object

problem_name: Minimum Distance of a Linear Code
canonical_encoding: a linear code over a finite field given by a generator or parity-check matrix; objective = the minimum Hamming weight of a nonzero codeword (the minimum distance)
simple directed graph; objective = a minimum-cardinality subset of the arcs that preserves all reachability relations (same transitive closure)
undirected graph with edge weights and an integer k (part of the input, no fixed terminals); objective = a minimum-weight set of edges whose removal leaves at least k connected components
a metric space (complete graph with metric edge lengths) and a start vertex; objective = a tour/path from the start minimizing the sum of arrival times (latencies) at the vertices
simple undirected graph; objective = a proper coloring by positive integers minimizing the SUM of the colors over all vertices (chromatic sum), not the number of colors
n items with sizes and m bins/machines (m part of the input); objective = assign every item to a bin minimizing the sum over bins of (bin load)^2, i.e. the squared L2 norm of the load vector
a set of items and a family of tests (each test is a subset of items); objective = a minimum-cardinality subfamily of tests that distinguishes every pair of items (some chosen test separates them)
a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane; objective = a triangulation (maximal set of non-crossing edges) minimizing the total edge length
a mixed graph (both undirected edges and directed arcs) with nonnegative lengths; objective = a minimum-length closed walk traversing every edge and arc at least once
undirected graph with edge weights and a set of source-sink terminal pairs; objective = a minimum-weight set of edges whose removal disconnects every terminal pair

n items each with a profit and a d-dimensional weight vector, and a d-dimensional capacity (d a fixed constant); objective = a subset of maximum total profit whose weight is within capacity in every dimension

k strings over a fixed alphabet and a metric on symbols (incl. gaps); objective = an alignment minimizing the sum-of-pairs (SP) score = sum over all pairs of sequences of their induced pairwise alignment cost
a linear code over GF(2) given by a generator matrix, and a target vector y; objective = a codeword minimizing the Hamming distance to y (maximum-likelihood decoding)
undirected graph and a set of >= 3 terminals; objective = a minimum-cardinality set of non-terminal vertices whose removal pairwise separates all terminals
n jobs and m machines (m part of the input); each job has one operation per machine, executable in any order but not concurrently; objective = minimize the makespan (O||Cmax)
a metric (undirected) graph with vertex rewards, a start (and optionally end) vertex, and a length budget B; objective = a walk of length <= B collecting the maximum total reward

simple undirected graph; a book embedding places vertices on a spine (linear order) and assigns each edge to a page so that same-page edges do not cross; objective = the minimum number of pages (book thickness)
simple undirected graph; objective = the minimum width over all path-decompositions (equivalently interval-completion clique number minus one / vertex separation number)

a 3-CNF formula whose variable-clause incidence graph is planar; decision object = satisfiability; optimization object (for the approximation charge) = MAX planar 3-SAT (maximize the number of satisfied clauses)
simple undirected graph; objective = a minimum set of vertices whose deletion makes the graph planar (the k-apex / vertex-planarization problem)

simple undirected graph; a vertex set observes by domination (a chosen vertex and its neighbors) plus a propagation rule (an observed vertex with all-but-one observed neighbors forces the last neighbor); objective = a minimum set observing all vertices
n unit-length jobs with a precedence DAG and m identical machines; objective = minimize the makespan subject to the precedence constraints (P|prec,pj=1|Cmax)

simple undirected graph with some vertices preassigned colors and a total color budget; decision = can the partial coloring be extended to a proper coloring of the whole graph using the given number of colors?
integers a, b, c in binary; decision: does there exist z <= c with z^2 ≡ a (mod b)?
n items with a knapsack constraint (weights + capacity, binary) and a nonnegative quadratic profit matrix (pairwise item profits); maximize total selected profit
simple undirected graph; an L(2,1)-labeling assigns integer labels so adjacent vertices differ by >=2 and distance-2 vertices differ by >=1; objective = minimum span (max label used)
an n x n array of nonnegative weights and an integer p; partition into at most p axis-parallel rectangular tiles minimizing the maximum tile weight
a set of terminal points in the plane under the rectilinear (L1) metric; minimum-length tree (Steiner points allowed) connecting all terminals
a set of red elements R, blue elements B, and a family S of subsets of R∪B; choose a subfamily covering every blue element while covering the fewest red elements
a directed acyclic graph (an expression/computation DAG); decision: can the DAG be evaluated using at most k registers (Sethi register-sufficiency / black pebble game)?
n unit/known-length jobs on m identical machines with s shared renewable resources (per-job resource demands, per-resource bounds); minimize makespan
simple undirected graph; a Roman dominating function assigns 0/1/2 to vertices so every 0-vertex is adjacent to a 2-vertex; objective = minimum total weight

a ground set and a family of subsets; a 2-coloring 'splits' a set if the set is not monochromatic. Feasibility: 2-color so every set is split (hypergraph 2-colorability). Optimization: maximize #split sets
a set of strings over a finite alphabet; find the shortest string that contains every input string as a (not necessarily contiguous) subsequence
an unsigned permutation; minimum number of segment reversals to transform it into the identity (genome rearrangement / reversal distance)
a permutation; minimum number of block transpositions (move a contiguous block to another position) to reach the identity (transposition distance)
a capacitated graph with a set of source-sink demand pairs; find a cut minimizing the ratio of cut capacity to separated demand (non-uniform sparsest cut)
a metric (triangle-inequality) space with a set of pickup->delivery arcs; a single server must traverse every arc in its given direction; minimize total tour length
a string over {H,P} (hydrophobic/polar); embed it as a self-avoiding walk on the 2D/3D square lattice maximizing the number of non-adjacent-in-sequence H-H lattice contacts
a set of axis-aligned rectangles and a strip of fixed width; pack them without rotation/overlap minimizing the total height used
a set of positive integers (binary) and a target P; decision: does some subset have product exactly P?
a graph with per-vertex thresholds; an initially active seed set activates a neighbor once its number of active neighbors reaches its threshold; find the minimum seed set activating the whole graph
simple undirected graph; minimum number of planar subgraphs into which the edge set can be partitioned
simple undirected graph; a total coloring properly colors vertices and edges together (adjacent/incident elements differ); objective = minimum number of colors (total chromatic number chi'')
simple undirected graph with no isolated vertex; a total dominating set S has every vertex (including those in S) adjacent to a vertex of S; objective = minimum |S|
simple undirected graph; find a maximum-cardinality set of pairwise vertex-disjoint triangles
a symmetric distance matrix D on n points; find a tree metric (additive tree) T minimizing the L-infinity error ||D - T||_inf (numerical taxonomy)
n jobs and m machines with a machine-dependent processing time p_ij for each job-machine pair; assign jobs to machines minimizing the makespan
a capacitated graph with source-sink demand pairs, each demand routed on a SINGLE path; maximize the total routed demand (throughput) respecting capacities
simple undirected graph; find a MAXIMUM-cardinality MINIMAL dominating set (the upper domination number Gamma(G))
n items, each a d-dimensional vector in [0,1]^d (d a fixed constant >= 2); pack into the minimum number of bins so that each bin's coordinate-wise vector sum is <= 1 in every dimension
a metric (triangle-inequality) space with a depot, client demands, and vehicle capacity Q; minimize the total length of depot-rooted routes each serving total demand <= Q

problem_name: Minimum Weighted Completion Time (identical machines, P||sum w_j C_j)
canonical_encoding: n jobs with processing times and weights, m identical parallel machines; minimize the weighted sum of job completion times sum_j w_j C_j

problem_name: Total Weighted Tardiness (single machine, 1||sum w_j T_j)
canonical_encoding: n jobs with processing times, weights, and due dates on one machine; minimize the total weighted tardiness sum_j w_j * max(0, C_j - d_j)
simple undirected graph, adjacency-list (n,m); count the acyclic orientations of G (= (-1)^n * chromatic polynomial P(G,-1) = Tutte T(G;2,0))

problem_name: #Antichains (count antichains / order ideals of a poset)
canonical_encoding: finite poset given by its comparability/Hasse DAG on n elements; count the antichains of P (equivalently the order ideals / down-sets, in bijection)

problem_name: #Contingency-Tables (count nonnegative integer matrices with prescribed margins)
canonical_encoding: row-sum vector r in N^m and column-sum vector c in N^n (entries in binary); count the m x n nonnegative-integer matrices with row sums r and column sums c

problem_name: #Eulerian-Circuits (count Eulerian circuits of an undirected graph)
canonical_encoding: connected UNDIRECTED (multi)graph with every vertex of even degree, adjacency-list; count the Eulerian circuits (closed trails using every edge exactly once, up to the usual starting-point/orientation convention)
connected UNDIRECTED graph with every vertex of even degree, adjacency-list; count the Eulerian orientations (orientations in which each vertex has indegree = outdegree)
finite poset given by its DAG (Hasse diagram) on n elements; count the linear extensions (total orders refining the partial order)

problem_name: #Matchings (count all matchings of a graph; monomer-dimer)
canonical_encoding: simple undirected graph, adjacency-list; count ALL matchings of every size (independent edge sets) = the monomer-dimer partition function at unit activity, sum over k of the k-matching numbers
monotone 2-CNF over n Boolean variables (each clause = OR of two POSITIVE literals); count the satisfying assignments
connected undirected (multi)graph, adjacency-list; count the spanning trees of G

problem_name: #DNF (count satisfying assignments of a DNF formula)
canonical_encoding: a DNF formula over n Boolean variables; count the number of satisfying assignments
